correctness.rationale: Conditioning on independent gamma increments U,V,Z and one shared pathwise gamma diffusivity D, Wick/Isserlis yields R=(M_L²+2(α+1)K_{L,g})/[3(α+1)N_L−αM_L²] with M=E v(U), N=E v(U)² and K=E c(U,Z,V)². For H>1/2 the positive decreasing tempered covariance C_H gives strictly declining K with g by gamma-subordinator coupling and a positive far-gap heterogeneous-diffusivity floor. Integration gives v(s)=a s−b+ρ(s) with exponentially decaying remainder; gamma Laplace transform gives M=aL−b+O(e^-cL), N−M²=a²L/η+O(Le^-cL), while bounded K is uniform g≥0. This yields R=1/(2α+3)−3(α+1)/((2α+3)²ηL)+O(L^-2) uniformly in gap. For fixed g dominated convergence K→Eρ(Z_g)²/4 yields the L^-2 gap signal and g=0 coefficient. Independently checked H=1 explicit kernel identities and large-L first/second coefficients numerically across several α,η,g. H<1 limit and parameter-uniformity are NOT claimed.
residual_risks: Quenched diffusivity shared across both windows is essential; choosing independent D by window would eliminate the plateau.

value.rationale: Two-window squared-increment volatility is a natural diagnostic distinguishing shared quenched heterogeneity from finite-range Gaussian memory. Exact gap-uniform L^-1 and gap-sensitive L^-2 coefficients quantify physically different effects in a well-defined stochastic transport model beyond its known one-time kurtosis.
residual_risks: The theorem describes the specified ideal stochastic process, not experiments or independent per-window diffusivities.

limitations: Fixed H>1/2, τ,α,η,β positive and D frozen per path; no parameter-uniform singular limit.
The H=1 numerical special case corroborates but does not prove 1/2<H<1.
